To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose a novel, 4D neural light field representation of the scene, 2) we show that the representation is efficient in terms of storage, and 3) we demonstrate that it enables real-time rendering and sparse depth map extraction from a single image.

* LFNs are a 360-degree four-dimensional neural implicit light field representation that enable single-evaluation rendering, and * LFNs can be meta-learned from single image observations of simple scenes and used for multi-view consistent light fields, sparse depth map extraction, and real-time rendering.
* LFNs are a new type of neural scene representation that can be rendered in real time with a single network evaluation per ray.
In summary, our research is concerned with

1) the representation of light fields via neural implicit representations; 2) the efficient rendering of light fields via single-evaluation ray tracing; and 3) the extraction of sparse 3D information from neural scene representations.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the 4D light field is a natural representation for neural scene representations, and that LFNs enable efficient rendering and learning from 2D images of scenes.
the LFN provides a novel neural scene prior that enables real-time rendering and efficient multi-view scene understanding.
neural implicit representations are not only a powerful tool for 3D scene representation, but can also enable efficient, single evaluation rendering of light fields.
